title: Prevalence of synovial changes in a study of joint health among healthy control subjects
summary:
The literature reports the prevalence of synovitis in adult patients with hemophilia at rates ranging from 26.9% to 67.8%. However, a precise comparison of these data with healthy control subjects is still pending. The reason for this is that the frequency of synovial changes in the healthy population, as determined using the examination methods established in hemophilia research, has not yet been sufficiently documented.

Although there are isolated data from osteoarthritis research describing synovial changes in the knee joint in up to 20.2% of healthy male subjects, the measurement methods used in those studies are not comparable to the methodological standards of hemophilia diagnostics.

The aim of this study is therefore to systematically assess the prevalence of synovitis in healthy control subjects using methods established in hemophilia research. This will create a valid reference basis that enables an objective and comparative evaluation of joint health in hemophilia patients.

interventions.name: In healthy male participants, the elbow, knee, and ankle joints are examined at a single time point using standardized ultrasound and clinical joint examinations. In addition, three standardized questionnaires are completed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
o Submission of written consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
o Individuals with acute (within the last 6 months) clinically significant joint pain or swelling.
o Individuals suffering from any of the following conditions:
- Blood clotting disorder
- Osteoarthritis
- Any rheumatic disease
- Individuals who have undergone any of the following previous surgeries:
- Arthroscopy
- Ligament reconstructions / ligament ruptures
- Meniscus injuries
- Joint replacement surgery
o Regular long-term NSAID therapy
o Intra-articular injections in the past 12 months
